title: A Mother's Song, a Priest's Downfall
overview: Hannah praises God for turning her life around, while the priest Eli's sons abuse their sacred role and a prophet announces that Eli's family will lose its place.

parts.label: Hannah's song of joy (vv. 1-3)
parts.note: Hannah celebrates that God has lifted her up after years of shame over being unable to have children; a raised "horn" is an image of strength and honor, taken from a strong animal's horns. Calling God a "Rock" means he is solid and dependable, and her warning to the proud is likely aimed first at her rival Peninnah, who had mocked her.

parts.label: God turns things upside down (vv. 4-10)
parts.note: The song widens into a picture of God reversing fortunes: the strong are weakened, the hungry are fed, the childless woman has many children, the poor are lifted from the ash heap to sit with princes. It ends with a hope for God's "anointed" king before Israel even had a king, and Christians later read this in light of Jesus (Messiah means "anointed one"); Mary's song in Luke 1 closely echoes it.

parts.label: Eli's sons rob the worshipers (vv. 11-17)
parts.note: In these offerings God's portion, the fat, was burned first, and the priests received set cuts, but Eli's sons grabbed whatever meat they wanted and even demanded it raw before God's part was offered, threatening force. The writer calls this a very great sin because it treated worship of God, and the people bringing it, with contempt.

parts.label: Samuel grows, Hannah is blessed (vv. 18-21)
parts.note: Meanwhile young Samuel serves faithfully, wearing a simple linen garment used in worship, and each year Hannah brings him a new robe she made herself. Eli blesses the family, and Hannah goes on to have five more children.

parts.label: Eli's weak warning (vv. 22-26)
parts.note: Eli hears that his sons are also sleeping with women who served at the worship tent (what these women's role was is unclear), and he scolds them, but they ignore him. The text bluntly says God had already decided to put them to death; how that fits with their own refusal is something readers have long wrestled with.

parts.label: Doom announced for Eli's family (vv. 27-36)
parts.note: A prophet tells Eli that by putting his sons above God, his family will lose its priestly role, its members will die young, and both sons will die on the same day. God promises a faithful priest instead, which many link to Zadok, who later replaced Eli's line under King Solomon, though some see Samuel here.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether Hannah's mention of God's "anointed" king is a direct prophecy of Jesus or a hope for Israel's coming kings that was later read in light of him.
think: Hannah's song says the proud get brought low and the overlooked get lifted up; where have you seen that happen in real life, and where have you seen it fail to happen?
